# Signal Advisory

> Independent technology broker based in Kansas City, Missouri. Signal Advisory audits and renegotiates business technology contracts — telecom, internet, cloud, phone, security, and mobile — to reduce cost and consolidate vendors. Clients pay Signal Advisory directly; carriers do not. This independence is what separates Signal Advisory from a master agent.

Founded and led by Brandon Murphy, Principal Advisor. Contact: brandon@signaladvise.com or 816-355-3350. Headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri; serves clients across the United States.

## Core pages

- [Homepage](https://signaladvise.com/): Company overview, services, differentiators, FAQ, and contact.
- [Services](https://signaladvise.com/services): Full description of the four service lines.
- [Audit request](https://signaladvise.com/audit): Free invoice review form. Send a recent business technology bill; receive a one-page marked-up audit identifying overspend, contract risks, and consolidation opportunities within five business days.

## What Signal Advisory does

- **Provider negotiation.** Direct negotiation with every major U.S. technology provider on the client's behalf. Rate is one variable; term length, exit rights, and rate-protection clauses move more money over the life of a contract. Most agents do not press for them.
- **Vendor consolidation.** Mid-market companies typically pay four to six providers for services that should sit with one or two. Engagement starts with a single-page inventory of every contract, renewal date, and monthly cost. From there the consolidation decisions get straightforward.
- **Telecom expense management (TEM).** Every invoice, audited against every contract, every month. Errors are disputed. Unused services retired. Credits land on the next bill. On a typical mid-market footprint, this work recovers three to six percent of annual telecom spend.
- **Ongoing advisory.** Hourly or monthly retainer covering the technology decisions a team makes between major engagements — renewals, architecture, vendor selection, contract structure. On call when the question comes up.

## How Signal Advisory is different from a master agent

- An independent technology broker (Signal Advisory) is paid by the client. Recommendations are aligned to the client.
- A master agent is paid by the carrier and is required to disclose that relationship. Their economic incentive is to place the client with the carrier that pays them most.
- Signal Advisory does not accept carrier commissions on the brokerage line of business.

## Pricing

- Contingency: percentage of documented annual savings, paid only after savings land.
- Monthly retainer: fixed monthly fee for ongoing advisory and TEM coverage.
- Hourly: project-based engagements.
- Free invoice audit with no commitment — submit a bill, receive a marked-up review.

## Common questions

- **What does an independent technology broker do?** Inventories every technology contract a business has, then puts providers in competition for the renewal. Result: lower cost, better terms, fewer vendors to manage. Paid by the client, not the carrier.
- **How much can a business save by auditing technology invoices?** A typical mid-market audit recovers three to six percent of annual telecom and technology spend. Small businesses commonly save 15 to 30 percent on a single internet or phone contract when put out to bid.
- **Do I need to switch carriers to work with Signal Advisory?** No. Many engagements end with the client staying on the incumbent carrier at materially better rates and terms. Leverage is in being willing to switch, not in actually switching.
- **How are independent brokers paid?** Directly by the client — contingency, monthly retainer, or hourly. No carrier commissions.
- **What is the difference between a technology broker and a master agent?** Master agents are paid by carriers and disclose that relationship. Independent brokers are paid by the client and have no carrier in the recommendation.

## Categories of vendors Signal Advisory audits

- **Internet / network:** Comcast Business, AT&T, Lumen, Google Fiber, Spectrum, Cox Business
- **Mobile / wireless:** Verizon, T-Mobile, AT&T Mobility
- **Voice / unified communications:** RingCentral, 8x8, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Nextiva
- **Payments and POS:** Square, Stripe, Toast, Clover
- **Cloud and productivity:** Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, AWS
